activity.title: ACTIVITY
agents.hint: Every launch opens in the repository above and carries the mission briefing. The red button turns the CLI's approval prompts off.
agents.notes.codex: Skips approvals AND the sandbox. Codex calls this one extremely dangerous itself.
agents.notes.hermes: --yolo is a global flag; it goes before the subcommand as well as after.
agents.notes.openclaw: OpenClaw has no single bypass flag: permission lives in `openclaw approvals` and `openclaw exec-policy`, which are persisted host state rather than a launch argument. The elevated button therefore only elevates the process — set the exec policy once, by hand.
agents.title: AGENTS
agents.writeConfig.hint: Creates .rolloutloud/agents.json (edit a CLI's flags) and allowlist.json (which commands an agent may run without you clicking).
app.elevated.detail: Every CLI and every fluid button started from here inherits administrative rights.
app.notElevated.detail: Elevated launches will offer to restart RolloutLoud through the OS prompt first.
buttons.hint: Commands an agent needs run but cannot run itself. It posts one to the bridge and it appears here. Anything matching allowlist.json the agent may also run on its own.
buttons.pendingAuto: Pending — on the allowlist, so the agent can also run this itself.
buttons.title: FLUID BUTTONS
elevation.advice: If this mission does not need administrative rights, launching unelevated is the better choice — the bypass flag works either way.
elevation.explain: A child process cannot hold more privilege than its parent, so the CLI would start with its approval prompts off but without administrative rights — and the difference only shows up later, when a privileged command fails.
elevation.headline: You asked to launch {0} elevated, but RolloutLoud itself is not.
elevation.title: RolloutLoud is not elevated
gate.description.placeholder: in your words: green on Windows, twice in a row, nothing skipped
gate.hint: Without a machine check, the agent decides for itself when it is done — and a tired agent decides that early. With one, RolloutLoud runs it, then runs it again from a clean process before believing it.
gate.title: Success gate
gate.useCommand: Decide it with a command (exit 0 means achieved)
housekeeping.hint: Every subagent round writes its task, its briefing and its full output to .rolloutloud/runs/. A project whose main agent fires ten a session produces thousands of folders in a month, so old ones are pruned on startup and finished missions are moved aside — archived, never deleted, because the ledger is the expensive part.
housekeeping.title: Disk
identity.attached: Attached. Agents may ask for it, naming the site — only for the sites you listed, and every request is recorded below and in identity-access.log.
identity.none: Nothing attached, so agents are told not to create accounts and not to invent an address to get past a sign-up. That is the default and it needs no action.
identity.title: Attached identity
identity.warning: Everything in that file becomes part of an agent's context, which means it reaches the model provider. A throwaway password for a disposable test account is what this is for. Payment details, a password you use anywhere real, recovery codes and API keys with spend attached are not.
ledger.hint: What has been ruled out. Fed back to every agent and every subagent, so a spent idea stays spent across restarts.
ledger.title: LEDGER
mission.hint: Write the outcome you want, not the steps. The agents read this before their first turn and are told that a failed attempt is an input to the next one, never a result to report back.
mission.none: No mission. Write the outcome you want above and start one — the agents read it before their first turn.
mission.open.hint: Several agents can work in this window at once, one mission each. Switching here changes which one 'active' means to an agent that does not name one.
mission.placeholder: make the integration suite pass on Windows, not just on my machine
mission.title: MISSION
offload.hint: For long grinds. The main session keeps the mission and the ledger and spends its window on judgement; each concrete action goes to a fresh subagent with a short briefing and returns a structured verdict. Stops the cost per action climbing with the hour.
offload.threshold: Only once the window gets expensive
offload.title: Subagent offload
scope.auth.placeholder: who authorised this, and under what reference
scope.hint: Leave this blank for local work — most missions need no boundary. Fill it in when the agent will touch something outside this machine and the boundary has to hold: a staging environment that must not reach production, one database and not the one beside it. Any declared command naming nothing in here is refused.
scope.title: Scope
scope.warning: Targets are declared but authorisation is blank. Record who approved touching these, and under what reference, before starting.
shutdown.hint: An agent can ask to close RolloutLoud when it is finished. The request is judged on the mission state, never on what the agent says — "I could not do it" arrives as Exhausted and is refused.
shutdown.title: Closing when done
shutdown.unattended: Let it close the window itself, with no click from me
shutdown.unattended.hint: Off by default. The gate decides whether the WORK is done; this decides whether you want the window gone as a result, and that second question is yours. Left off, a button appears instead.
stop.hint: Relentless needs a brake, or it is just an unbounded spend that runs all night. Reaching one of these ends the mission as Exhausted, which is the budget working, not the agent failing.
stop.title: Stop conditions
theme.toDark: Switch to the dark theme. Remembered for you, not for this repository.
theme.toLight: Switch to the light theme. Remembered for you, not for this repository.
watchdog.barren: {0} rounds produced nothing. Stopping — that is a broken setup, not a hard problem.
watchdog.enable: Restart the agent when it stops early
watchdog.hint: Runs the agent itself and restarts it when it stops early. An agent that writes "let me know if you'd like me to try another approach" has decided it is finished — the watchdog disagrees, and hands it back the ledger and the current tier.
watchdog.relay: Hand the mission to a different CLI when this one runs out of ideas
watchdog.relay.hint: Tier 3 of the ladder, and the rung with the best return: the same objective and the same ledger handed to a different model regularly finds what the first could not, because the failure was in one model's habits. The outgoing agent writes a paragraph on what it came to believe and which of its own assumptions it stopped trusting.
watchdog.title: Watchdog
